title: The task
body: For every number, find the next greater number to its right (−1 if none). The stack holds the numbers still waiting for an answer; from bottom to top it always decreases.

title: Read 2 (i = 0)
body: 2 arrives. The stack is empty, so 2 is pushed and waits.

title: Read 7 (i = 1)
body: 7 arrives. It is greater than 2 on top of the stack, so it answers it and it is popped. Then 7 is pushed to wait for its own answer.

title: Read 3 (i = 2)
body: 3 arrives. It is not greater than the top of the stack (7), so nothing is answered; 3 is pushed and waits.

title: Read 5 (i = 3)
body: 5 arrives. It is greater than 3 on top of the stack, so it answers it and it is popped. Then 5 is pushed to wait for its own answer.

predict.question: The stack is [7, 3] and 5 arrives. What happens?
options: 3 is popped and answered with 5, then 5 is pushed: [7, 5]
predict.explanation: 5 > 3, so 5 is 3's next greater number. 5 < 7, so 7 keeps waiting. The stack stays decreasing: [7, 5].

title: Read 4 (i = 4)
body: 4 arrives. It is not greater than the top of the stack (5), so nothing is answered; 4 is pushed and waits.

title: Read 6 (i = 5)
body: 6 arrives. It is greater than 4, 5 on top of the stack, so it answers them and they are popped. Then 6 is pushed to wait for its own answer.

predict.question: The stack is [7, 5, 4] and 6 arrives. How many numbers does 6 answer?
predict.explanation: 6 > 4 and 6 > 5, so both are popped and answered with 6; 6 < 7 stops the loop.

title: Read 8 (i = 6)
body: 8 arrives. It is greater than 6, 7 on top of the stack, so it answers them and they are popped. Then 8 is pushed to wait for its own answer.

title: Leftovers
body: The numbers still on the stack never met a greater number, so their answer is −1. Each number was pushed once and popped at most once: **O(n)** time.
code: // whatever is left on the stack gets -1
